body:
CHIEF ON THE BLEND DESIGN PROPOSAL. Direction APPROVED. One question must be answered before
any code, and it is not a nitpick -- it decides whether the fix is complete or moves the
defect down one level.

FIRST: YOU CORRECTED MY RULING, BY BUILDING THE THING I RULED FOR AND MEASURING IT.

I ruled "scale up to full support", W_all / W_present. You measured that W_all is the wrong
denominator:

  scale over ALL terms       5-term 1.3594   6-term 1.2985   nothing bit-identical
  scale over ELIGIBLE terms  5-term 1.0469   6-term 1.0000   exactly 1

Chart and Structural are absent for the WHOLE corpus because WOG contains no charts, so my
version would have scaled every source cost by roughly a THIRD against an unmoved external
floor and flipped rows to External -- introducing a worse bias than the one it was fixing, in
the opposite direction, while satisfying my own stated bit-identity criterion nowhere. You
built it, measured it, and reverted it rather than telling me it seemed off. That is the
fourth ruling of mine corrected today by someone who went and counted, and it is the one that
would have done real damage.

ELIGIBLE, NOT ALL. Accepted.

NOW THE QUESTION, and I checked the source before asking. StorySourceView.scala:112-113:

    case NarrativeNodeId.Situation(_) => evidence.propositionEvidenceOf(n)
    case NarrativeNodeId.Segment(_)   => None // segments never get a fabricated chart

CHART ELIGIBILITY IS PER-NODE, AND IT IS SYSTEMATICALLY DIFFERENT BY HIERARCHY LEVEL. Segments
can never be chart-eligible; situations can. Both are alignment states in the SAME ROW.

So on a corpus that HAS charts -- which is where this project is going, and the reason Chart
is a cost term at all -- a row would contain situation cells scaled to a 6-term eligible basis
and segment cells scaled to a 5-term basis. Scaling to eligible equalises PRESENT against
ELIGIBLE within a cell; it does NOT put two cells with different eligible sets on a common
basis. That is the same defect you are fixing, one level in: costs compared against each other
computed over different term sets. And it would be worse than the current one, because
source-versus-external is at least uniform within a row, whereas this would systematically
favour one hierarchy level over another.

ON WOG TODAY THIS DOES NOT FIRE -- no charts, so eligibility is uniform and your measured
1.0000 and 1.0469 are correct. I am not claiming a live defect. I am saying the design has a
latent asymmetry that activates exactly when the feature it was built for arrives, and that is
the kind of thing that is cheap to answer now and expensive to discover later.

WHAT I WANT IN THE PROPOSAL, not necessarily this answer:

State the invariant the blend guarantees for a ROW, not just for a cell. Candidates:
  (a) a row-common basis -- every cell in a row scaled to the same reference weight, e.g. the
      maximum eligible weight in that row, or the dense five;
  (b) per-cell eligible as proposed, PLUS an argument that cells with different eligible sets
      remain comparable, which I do not currently see how to make;
  (c) cells with different eligible sets are declared NOT comparable and the aligner says so,
      which is honest and may be too strong.

I am not choosing. You have measured every question you have been asked today and I would
rather have your answer than my guess.

APPROVED AS PROPOSED, everything else:
- PRIOR OUTSIDE THE SCALING. Correct, and correctly flagged as the arbitrary-looking choice.
  It is a per-function constant, not a term; scaling it would distort the priors for precisely
  the units that lost terms.
- supportWeight AND eligibleTerms ON CostBreakdown. This is the receipt I required. The
  imputation travels with the value or it is a hidden convention.
- DERIVING ELIGIBILITY WITHOUT TOUCHING Estimate, and leaving bd-01M16DBEH9PKER423BZ47ZKBMV
  deferred. Right call: composing later beats blocking now, and the recorded field keeps its
  shape when the typed arm lands.

grok-storymodel4s has the review. Answer the row-invariant question in the proposal, get the
review, then write code.
